newsitem.title: ZAMBIA: Zambia courts close as magistrates strike over pay.
newsitem.headline: Zambia courts close as magistrates strike over pay.

text.p: Courts in the Zambian capital Lusaka were closed on Wednesday after magistrates and local court justices went on strike over pay demands.
They went on strike on Tuesday after the government failed to increase their wages as promised last year. Cases have been postponed indefinitely, court officials said.
High court registrar Timothy Katanekwa told Reuters the finance ministry was expected to act on the strikers' demands and the strike could be called off soon.

The Magistrates and Judges Association of Zambia said in a statement its striking members would not return to work until they had been granted better conditions of service. It refused to disclose the strikers' demands.
"The magistrates and local court justices have been prompted to take the action after several attempts for an amicable settlement have failed," the association said.
